::: {.route-question}
Question for today: what share of the cells CellCo starts ends up good, and which improvement buys the most yield per yuan?

## The cell's journey {#line}

::: {.two}
::: {}
Every cell passes **Formation (F)** and the **Aging test (A)**. A cell that fails goes to **Rework (R)** and is tested again. It ends either **Good (G)** or **Scrap (S)**.

G and S are **absorbing** states: once there, a cell never leaves. F, A and R are **transient**.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>From \ To</th><th class="num">F</th><th class="num">A</th><th class="num">R</th><th class="num">G</th><th class="num">S</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>F</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0.95</td><td class="num">0.03</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0.02</td></tr>
    <tr><td>A</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0.05</td><td class="num">0.92</td><td class="num">0.03</td></tr>
    <tr><td>R</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0.80</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0.20</td></tr>
    <tr><td>G</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">1</td><td class="num">0</td></tr>
    <tr><td>S</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">0</td><td class="num">1</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
:::
:::

[Rates are fictional, written for the CellCo case.]{.source}

## Three matrices answer three questions {#canonical}

```{=html}
<div class="formula"><p><i>P</i> = [ <i>Q</i> &nbsp;<i>R</i> ; 0 &nbsp;<i>I</i> ] &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>N</i> = (<i>I</i> − <i>Q</i>)<sup>−1</sup> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>B</i> = <i>N R</i> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; <i>t</i> = <i>N</i> · 1</p></div>
```

::: {.elements}
::: {.el}
[*Q*, transient to transient]{.label}
The 3 × 3 block among F, A and R.
:::
::: {.el}
[*N*, fundamental matrix]{.label}
Expected number of visits to each transient state.
:::
::: {.el}
[*B* = *NR*]{.label}
Probability of ending in each absorbing state, Good or Scrap.
:::
::: {.el .key}
[*t* = *N*1]{.label}
Expected number of steps before absorption.
:::
:::

[Why N? A cell can visit A once, twice or more. N = I + Q + Q² + ... adds up all those paths.]{.note-line}

## What happens to a cell that enters formation {#results}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Starting in F</th><th class="num">Value</th><th>Meaning</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>P(Good) = <i>B</i>(F, G)</td><td class="num hit">0.933</td><td>93.3% of started cells end good</td></tr>
    <tr><td>P(Scrap) = <i>B</i>(F, S)</td><td class="num">0.067</td><td>6.7% are scrapped</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Visits to A, <i>N</i>(F, A)</td><td class="num">1.015</td><td>101.5 aging tests per 100 started cells</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Visits to R, <i>N</i>(F, R)</td><td class="num">0.081</td><td>8.1 reworks per 100 started cells</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Steps to absorption, <i>t</i>(F)</td><td class="num">2.095</td><td>about two process steps per cell</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

[A cell that is already in rework ends good with probability only 0.767, against 0.958 for a cell entering the aging test.]{.note-line}

## In Excel {#excel}

```{=html}
<pre class="code-slide"><span><b class="c">B2:D4   Q       </b> the 3 × 3 block: rows F, A, R and columns F, A, R</span><span><b class="c">F2:G4   R       </b> the 3 × 2 block: columns Good, Scrap</span><span><b class="c">B7:D9   I − Q   </b> =IF(ROW()-ROW($B$7)=COLUMN()-COLUMN($B$7),1,0)-B2   (copy across the block)</span><span><b class="c">B12:D14 N       </b> =MINVERSE(B7:D9)</span><span><b class="c">F12:G14 B       </b> =MMULT(B12:D14, F2:G4)</span><span><b class="c">H12:H14 t       </b> =MMULT(B12:D14, {1;1;1})</span></pre>
```

## Activity 1 · Answer {#act1-answer}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>B, probability of ending</th><th class="num">Good</th><th class="num">Scrap</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>from F</td><td class="num">0.933</td><td class="num">0.067</td></tr>
    <tr><td>from A</td><td class="num">0.958</td><td class="num">0.042</td></tr>

  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
With rework success at 0.90, the yield from F rises to **0.941**. A cell in rework faces a 20% chance of scrap before it even returns to the test, so its yield is low.
:::

## Three ways to raise yield {#improve}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Option</th><th>Change in the matrix</th><th class="num">Cost, CNY million</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>(a) Better formation control</td><td>F → S from 0.02 to 0.01 (F → A 0.96)</td><td class="num">1.2</td></tr>
    <tr><td>(b) Rework training</td><td>R → A from 0.80 to 0.90 (R → S 0.10)</td><td class="num">0.6</td></tr>
    <tr><td>(c) Fewer false rejects in the aging test</td><td>A → R from 0.05 to 0.03 (A → G 0.94)</td><td class="num">0.9</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
CellCo starts 6.25 million cells a year (2 GWh at 0.32 kWh per cell), and each good cell contributes CNY 25. One percentage point of yield is worth about **CNY 1.56 million a year**.
:::

## Try a change {#yield-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="yx">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">F → Scrap <strong id="yx-fs-v">0.02</strong><input type="range" id="yx-fs" min="0" max="0.06" step="0.005" value="0.02"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">A → Rework <strong id="yx-ar-v">0.05</strong><input type="range" id="yx-ar" min="0" max="0.12" step="0.005" value="0.05"></label>
    <label class="w-slider">Rework success <strong id="yx-rs-v">0.80</strong><input type="range" id="yx-rs" min="0.5" max="1" step="0.01" value="0.8"></label>
  </div>
  <table class="wide" id="yx-t"></table>
  <div class="w-readout" id="yx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('yx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  function inv3(m) {
    const [a, b, c] = m[0], [d, e, f] = m[1], [g, h, i] = m[2];
    const A = e * i - f * h, B = -(d * i - f * g), C = d * h - e * g, det = a * A + b * B + c * C;
    return [[A, -(b * i - c * h), b * f - c * e], [B, a * i - c * g, -(a * f - c * d)], [C, -(a * h - b * g), a * e - b * d]].map((r) => r.map((x) => x / det));
  }
  function model(fs, ar, rs) {
    // F: 0.03 to rework fixed, the rest of what is not scrap goes to A. A: 0.03 scrap fixed.
    const Q = [[0, 1 - 0.03 - fs, 0.03], [0, 0, ar], [0, rs, 0]], R = [[0, fs], [1 - ar - 0.03, 0.03], [0, 1 - rs]];
    const I_Q = Q.map((r, i) => r.map((x, j) => (i === j ? 1 : 0) - x)), N = inv3(I_Q);
    const B = N.map((r) => [0, 1].map((k) => r.reduce((s, x, j) => s + x * R[j][k], 0)));
    return { N, B };
  }
  const base = model(0.02, 0.05, 0.8).B[0][0];
  function draw() {
    const fs = +document.getElementById('yx-fs').value, ar = +document.getElementById('yx-ar').value, rs = +document.getElementById('yx-rs').value;
    document.getElementById('yx-fs-v').textContent = fs.toFixed(3); document.getElementById('yx-ar-v').textContent = ar.toFixed(3); document.getElementById('yx-rs-v').textContent = rs.toFixed(2);
    const { N, B } = model(fs, ar, rs), y = B[0][0], gain = y - base, value = gain * 6.25e6 * 25 / 1e6;
    document.getElementById('yx-t').innerHTML = '<thead><tr><th>Starting in F</th><th class="num">Yield</th><th class="num">Scrap</th><th class="num">Aging tests per 100 cells</th><th class="num">Reworks per 100 cells</th></tr></thead>' +
      `<tbody><tr><td>This setting</td><td class="num hit">${y.toFixed(4)}</td><td class="num">${B[0][1].toFixed(4)}</td><td class="num">${(N[0][1] * 100).toFixed(1)}</td><td class="num">${(N[0][2] * 100).toFixed(1)}</td></tr></tbody>`;
    document.getElementById('yx-out').innerHTML = `Change from today's 0.9334: <b>${gain >= 0 ? '+' : '−'}${Math.abs(gain * 100).toFixed(2)} points</b>, worth <span class="best">CNY ${value >= 0 ? '' : '−'}${Math.abs(value).toFixed(2)} million a year</span>.`;
  }
  ['yx-fs', 'yx-ar', 'yx-rs'].forEach((id) => document.getElementById(id).addEventListener('input', draw));
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

[Set one slider to an option's new value, read the gain, then reset it before trying the next option.]{.hint}

## Activity 2 · Yield investment pitch {#act2 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Groups of 4 · 30 minutes · the widget and a calculator]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Your group has CNY 2 million. Choose one or more of options (a), (b) and (c) within the budget, and pitch your choice to the board in 2 minutes.
:::

1. For each option, find the yield gain and its value per year. Which option gives the most yield per yuan?
2. Which combination within CNY 2 million gives the largest gain? Combined effects are not simply additive: check them with the widget.
3. State the payback time and one risk that could make your estimate wrong.

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: rank the three options by gain per yuan before you go on.
:::

## Activity 2 · Answer {#act2-answer}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Choice</th><th class="num">Cost</th><th class="num">Yield</th><th class="num">Gain, points</th><th class="num">Value, CNY million/yr</th><th class="num">Points per CNY million</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>(a) formation</td><td class="num">1.2</td><td class="num">0.9430</td><td class="num">0.96</td><td class="num">1.50</td><td class="num">0.80</td></tr>
    <tr><td>(b) rework</td><td class="num">0.6</td><td class="num">0.9412</td><td class="num">0.78</td><td class="num">1.22</td><td class="num hit">1.30</td></tr>
    <tr><td>(c) aging test</td><td class="num">0.9</td><td class="num">0.9381</td><td class="num">0.47</td><td class="num">0.73</td><td class="num">0.52</td></tr>
    <tr><td>(a) + (b)</td><td class="num">1.8</td><td class="num">0.9508</td><td class="num hit">1.74</td><td class="num hit">2.72</td><td class="num">0.97</td></tr>
    <tr><td>(b) + (c)</td><td class="num">1.5</td><td class="num">0.9439</td><td class="num">1.04</td><td class="num">1.63</td><td class="num">0.69</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.bridge}
Buy (a) and (b): CNY 1.8 million adds 1.74 points of yield, worth CNY 2.72 million a year, so it pays back in about 8 months. Option (b) alone gives the most yield per yuan.
:::

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
An absorbing chain splits into Q and R. N = (I − Q)^−1^ counts visits, and B = NR gives the chance of ending good or scrapped.
:::
::: {.tk}
CellCo's line turns 93.3% of started cells into good cells, with 8 reworks per 100 cells.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
Compare improvements on the same model and the same unit, yield per yuan. Combined changes interact, so test them together.
:::
:::
